analyses.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: Closed the session at a fresh 52-week high with a tight base behind it — the single cleanest large-cap setup in the scan, and the flagship of the financials leadership that ran this tape.

financials.summary: Another record year. Managed revenue set an all-time high on the back of a net interest income line that held up far better than the bank guided at the start of the year, plus a genuine rebound in the capital-markets franchise — Markets revenue and investment-banking fees both recovered as deal activity reopened. Credit costs normalized rather than deteriorated: card net charge-offs drifted toward the mid-3% range as expected, while reserve builds stayed modest and consumer delinquency formation stabilized. Expenses grew, but on technology and bankers rather than on remediation, so operating leverage stayed positive. The balance sheet ended the year over-capitalized, with CET1 comfortably above requirement, which is why the buyback ran hard through the back half.
highlights: Record managed revenue and record net income for the full year — the franchise's fourth consecutive record
Net interest income beat the conservative guide set in early 2025 as deposit repricing pressure faded
Investment banking fees and Markets revenue both up double digits as the deal window reopened
Return on tangible common equity again in the high teens — best-in-class among the money-center banks
CET1 ratio well above the regulatory minimum, funding an aggressive buyback and a raised dividend
Credit normalized, not cracked: card charge-offs rose to a mid-cycle range with no reserve shock

accomplishments: Held the #1 or #2 position in global investment banking fees for the year
Grew deposits and gained share in consumer banking while regional peers were still shrinking
Cleanly absorbed and integrated the First Republic book, which is now a contributor rather than a drag
Passed the annual stress test with a comfortable buffer, enabling a dividend increase and expanded repurchase authorization
Continued to lead the group on technology spend, with an AI deployment across research, ops and coding at real scale

journey_52w.summary: A grinding, low-drama advance from roughly the $280 area to a 52-week high at $365 — about +30% over three months alone and, critically, a move that came with the whole banking group rather than in isolation. The stock spent the spring building a shallow, tight base above a rising 50-day moving average, then broke out as the rate outlook stabilized and the capital-markets recovery became undeniable. There was no blow-off phase: the 4-contraction VCP pattern the scanner flagged is the fingerprint of steady institutional accumulation rather than a momentum chase.

analyses.name: Bank of America Corporation
analyses.verdict: Top-scoring name in the entire 542-ticker scan and a TradingView STRONG BUY, closing at a 52-week high — but with an RSI near 75 on below-average volume it is the most extended of the big banks, which makes it a pullback buy rather than a chase.

financials.summary: The year BAC's rate story finally turned in its favour. The bank spent 2023–24 carrying a low-yielding securities portfolio bought at the wrong time; through 2025 those positions rolled off and were reinvested at materially higher yields, so net interest income inflected upward each quarter rather than grinding down. Consumer banking held deposit share with unusually low-cost funding, and the Global Markets business put up its strongest full year on record as trading conditions stayed favourable. Expense discipline was real — headcount was roughly flat while revenue grew — and credit stayed contained, with commercial real estate reserves proving adequate against a book that the market had feared. Capital returns stepped up meaningfully in the second half.
highlights: Net interest income inflected higher through the year as the securities-portfolio drag rolled off — the central thesis of the stock, now proven
Record full-year Global Markets revenue, with sales and trading up on both the equity and fixed-income sides
Roughly 34% EPS growth and 17% revenue growth in the trailing data, an unusual combination for a bank this size
Deposit costs among the lowest in the peer group — the consumer franchise's structural advantage
Commercial real estate losses came in below the bear case; reserves were built ahead of the problem
Expanded buyback authorization and a dividend increase after a comfortable stress-test result

accomplishments: Delivered the NII inflection management had promised for two years, which was the bull case's entire load-bearing wall
Grew the Global Markets franchise to a record year without a corresponding jump in risk-weighted assets
Held roughly flat headcount while growing revenue, producing genuine positive operating leverage
Navigated the commercial real estate cycle without the credit event the market had priced in during 2024
Continued digital-banking share gains, with the large majority of consumer transactions now digital

journey_52w.summary: From roughly $46 to a 52-week high of $64.82 — a near-doubling off the low end of the range and up about 31% in three months, closing the session at the very top of its 52-week range. The path was a textbook stair-step: a base, a break, a shallow consolidation, then another leg. The scanner flags a 4-contraction VCP with the stock making a relative-strength new high, meaning it is not just going up, it is going up faster than the market. What it also means is that the easy part is over — RSI closed near 75.

analyses.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
analyses.verdict: Closed at an all-time high with the strongest fundamental momentum in the scan — triple-digit EPS growth against an 11x forward multiple — and it is the one leadership group that is not financials.

financials.summary: A refining upcycle year, and MPC's operating leverage did what it does. Crack spreads widened materially through the year as global refining capacity stayed tight — closures in Europe and the US ran ahead of new capacity additions — while demand for distillate in particular held firm. MPC's Gulf Coast and Mid-Continent systems ran at high utilization, and the company's scale in the largest US refining footprint meant the margin expansion dropped through to earnings almost undiluted. The MPLX midstream stake continued to throw off a steady, fee-based distribution that cushions the cyclicality. Free cash flow was enormous and management did the same thing it has done every year: bought back stock aggressively, shrinking the share count and levering the per-share numbers further.
highlights: EPS growth of roughly 348% and revenue growth of about 54% in the trailing data — the operating leverage of a refiner in an up-cycle

MPLX midstream distributions provided a large, fee-based, non-cyclical cash stream

Forward P/E of roughly 11x despite the earnings surge, because the market refuses to capitalize refining earnings

accomplishments: Ran the largest US refining system at high utilization through a demanding year
Sustained one of the most aggressive buyback programs in the S&P 500 relative to market cap
Grew MPLX distributions, strengthening the cash cushion under the cyclical refining earnings
Reached an all-time high share price alongside peer PSX, confirming a genuine group move rather than a single-name story

analyses.name: Arista Networks, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The best-looking technology setup in the scan — a 52-week high, a relative-strength new high, and roughly 50% three-month momentum — and notably the one AI-infrastructure name that did not participate in the sector's drawdown.

financials.summary: Arista remained the pure-play beneficiary of AI data-center networking build-outs, and the year's numbers reflected it. Revenue growth stayed strong as the largest cloud and AI customers moved from pilot clusters to production-scale deployments, where high-radix, low-latency Ethernet switching is the requirement. The company's insistence on Ethernet over InfiniBand for AI back-end networks — a contrarian call two years ago — became the industry default, and Arista's 800G product cycle landed into that demand. Gross margins stayed structurally high for a hardware company because the value sits in the EOS software layer rather than the box, and operating margin expanded as revenue outgrew opex. The balance sheet remained debt-free with a very large net cash position.
highlights: Roughly 38% revenue growth and 36% EPS growth in the trailing data — rare acceleration at this revenue scale
AI back-end networking moved from pilots to production deployments at the largest cloud customers
Ethernet won the AI networking architecture argument, which was Arista's explicit strategic bet
800G product cycle shipped into peak demand

accomplishments: Took durable data-center switching share from the incumbent while growing the overall market
Established Ethernet as the standard for AI back-end networks, displacing the proprietary alternative
Scaled 800G deployments with the largest hyperscale and AI-native customers
Sustained high-30s revenue growth at multi-billion scale without margin erosion

The important context is what it did relative to its neighbourhood: while ORCL sits 53% below its high, WDC 39% below, GLW 35% below and AMD 17% below, Arista closed at a new high. That divergence is the tell — capital leaving speculative AI-infrastructure exposure is still paying for the part of the build-out with visible, invoiced revenue. The scanner shows a 4-contraction VCP and a relative-strength new high on above-average volume, which is the highest-quality combination in the entire technology cohort here.

analyses.name: NVIDIA Corporation
analyses.verdict: Scores 92.9 and sits only 4.8% below its high with a 17x forward multiple, but earnings land in 15 days — that binary event is the reason this is a watch rather than a buy tonight.

financials.summary: The Blackwell cycle year. Revenue growth stayed extraordinary as the platform ramped into full production and data-center revenue continued to dominate the mix, with the networking attach — the switching and interconnect sold alongside the GPUs — becoming a material business in its own right. Gross margins compressed modestly during the steepest part of the ramp, as they always do when a new architecture enters volume production, then recovered as yields matured. The trailing figures in the scan show roughly 215% EPS growth on about 85% revenue growth, which is the operating leverage of a company whose costs are largely fixed against a supply-constrained product. Cash generation was immense and funded a very large buyback alongside strategic investments across the AI ecosystem.

analyses.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The mega-cap that is actually working — 5.9% below its high with a 92.1 score while AAPL sits 11% below, GOOGL 15% below and ORCL 53% below.

financials.summary: The margin story finally overtook the growth story. AWS reaccelerated as AI workloads moved into production and the segment's operating margin stayed at high levels, while the retail business — the part investors spent a decade forgiving — turned into a genuine profit engine as the regionalized US fulfilment network and same-day delivery build-out drove cost-to-serve down for a third consecutive year. Advertising continued compounding at a rate that would make it a large-cap standalone business, at incremental margins that flatter the whole. The trailing data shows roughly 242% EPS growth on about 20% revenue growth, which is the signature of a company whose revenue grew moderately while its cost structure improved dramatically. Capital expenditure remained enormous and directed at AI capacity, which is the bear case's ammunition.
highlights: Roughly 20% revenue growth converting to about 242% EPS growth — operating leverage, not top-line heroics

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: Within 1.2% of its 52-week high with 20% three-month momentum — the healthcare sector's clear leader, and a genuine diversifier away from the financials and energy trade that dominates the rest of this list.

financials.summary: The incretin franchise carried the company to one of the largest revenue increases in pharmaceutical history. Tirzepatide across both its diabetes and obesity indications scaled dramatically as manufacturing capacity — the binding constraint for two straight years — finally caught up with demand, and the trailing data's roughly 48% revenue growth reflects supply being unlocked rather than demand being created. Gross margins are structurally high, and the operating leverage was tempered only by deliberate reinvestment: Lilly spent heavily on capacity expansion and on an unusually broad late-stage pipeline. The oral incretin programme advanced toward commercialization, which matters because an oral formulation addresses the manufacturing and cold-chain constraints that limit injectables.

analyses.name: GE Aerospace
analyses.verdict: A high-quality industrial 4.2% below its high with an RSI of 60.6 — un-extended, well-supported, and riding an aftermarket cycle that has years left in it.

financials.summary: The first full year as a focused aerospace pure-play, and the model worked as advertised. The economics of this business are in services rather than equipment: engines are sold at thin or negative margin and the money is made over decades of spare parts and shop visits. With the global fleet flying more hours than ever and airlines deferring fleet replacement because new aircraft deliveries remain constrained, older engines stayed in service longer and generated more shop visits — precisely the high-margin aftermarket revenue GE monetizes. The trailing data shows roughly 21% revenue growth and 19% EPS growth, with margin expansion driven by that services mix. Free cash flow conversion was strong and supported both buybacks and a rising dividend.

analyses.name: Ross Stores, Inc.
analyses.verdict: One of the three highest-scoring names in the scan and a genuine consumer diversifier, but earnings land in nine days and RSI closed near 72 — worth owning, worth sizing for the event.

financials.summary: Off-price retail did what it does when the consumer trades down: it took share. Comparable-store sales grew steadily as shoppers migrated from full-price apparel retailers, and the merchandise-margin picture improved as the buying organization capitalized on abundant closeout availability — when full-price retailers over-order, Ross's inventory gets cheaper. The trailing data shows roughly 21% revenue growth and 37% EPS growth, an unusually strong combination for a mature retailer and a clear sign that margin, not just traffic, is driving results. Store expansion continued at a measured pace and the company returned substantial cash through buybacks and a rising dividend.

analyses.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
analyses.verdict: The only large semiconductor TradingView rates STRONG BUY while it rates AMD, NXPI and WDC outright SELL — and at 10% below its high with RSI 56.4, it is the un-extended way to own the AI supply chain.

financials.summary: A year defined by leading-edge scarcity. Advanced nodes — the 3nm and 5nm families — became the overwhelming majority of wafer revenue as AI accelerators, high-end smartphones and datacenter CPUs all competed for the same constrained capacity. Because TSMC is effectively the only foundry able to manufacture at the leading edge in volume, that scarcity translated into pricing power it has historically been reluctant to exercise, and gross margins expanded despite the enormous cost of new fabs and the dilution from overseas expansion in Arizona, Japan and Germany. Advanced packaging, particularly CoWoS, was its own bottleneck and its own profit centre: the capacity to package AI accelerators became as scarce as the silicon itself. Capital expenditure remained extraordinary, which is the cost of maintaining a monopoly at the leading edge.

analyses.name: SpaceX
analyses.verdict: A recent listing, so lead with the thesis rather than the quant signals — the scanner has barely a year of history to work with and the pattern scores are close to meaningless. TradingView rates it STRONG BUY with 10 buy signals and zero sells, which is notable given how rarely new listings get a clean read at all.

financials.period: Most recent full fiscal year as a newly public company
financials.summary: Treat every number here with more caution than usual: as a recent listing, the reporting history is short and the comparability of prior-period figures is limited. The economics rest on two very different engines. The launch business is the world's dominant provider of orbital lift by mass and by cadence, with reusability having driven marginal launch cost far below any competitor — that business is mature, cash-generative and effectively without a peer at scale. The satellite-broadband business is the growth engine and the capital sink: subscriber growth has been rapid across consumer, maritime, aviation and government segments, but the constellation requires continuous replenishment, and the capital intensity of maintaining thousands of short-lived satellites is the central question for the equity. Government and defence contracts provide a high-quality, contracted revenue floor beneath both.

Reusability has driven marginal launch economics far below any competing provider
